priority: DOT first; public HTTPS images before licensed feeds

providers.notes: Public no-charge HTTPS files documented for third-party integration; preserve attribution and review image ownership. Districts 01-12; D04 covers San Francisco. A listed image URL does not prove a current frame.

providers.media: HTTPS PNG snapshots; HLS may be available
providers.notes: VDOT officially requires an Iteris-managed third-party user agreement for integrated 511 traffic video, including free-distribution use. Public map metadata and media URLs do not establish redistribution authorization. Contact 511_videosubscription@iteris.com; do not enable playback without documented approval.

providers.media: Public video URL per camera; image compatibility not verified
providers.notes: Maryland iMAP exposes GIS camera ID, location, latitude/longitude, and public camera URL, but the layer metadata alone does not certify footage is current, accessible as a JPEG, or licensed for embedding. Keep media gated until reviewed. Maryland's separate Socrata JSON endpoint contains individual camera names, point locations and publisher video.php pages. These HTML player URLs are not direct image streams.
WSDOT documents an AccessCode parameter; never hardcode a key in public Rust-Boy state or repository.
NYC DOT explicitly requires a signed data-sharing agreement for developers; do not embed camera URLs before agreement.
A registered developer key and rate limits apply; do not ship credentials in catalog or browser state.
MassDOT directs third-party camera API access through TrafficLand sales@trafficland.com. No anonymous Boston camera URL is approved.

Official DDOT GIS layer 2 provides CameraID, Location, Latitude, Longitude, and Operation_Status (0 inactive/1 active). It contains no media URL. Location/status data may be indexed; never infer a video feed.

providers.coverage: Hartford, New Haven, Stamford, Bridgeport, Waterbury and CT interstates
providers.notes: CTroads documents a developer key and throttling of 10 calls per 60 seconds. Do not scrape its public camera page or ship a key.

providers.coverage: Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Harrisburg, Allentown, Scranton and PA interstates
providers.media: Near-real-time traffic images and licensed streams
providers.notes: PennDOT requires a data feed request, sharing terms and a nonexclusive video sharing license for camera streams. No unauthorized direct embeds.

providers.coverage: Newark, Jersey City, Trenton, Atlantic City and NJ turnpikes
providers.media: Traffic camera images refreshed about every 30 seconds in public viewer
providers.notes: NJDOT documents publicly viewed image cameras, but direct reuse/embedding API and camera coordinates need confirmation.

providers.coverage: Providence, Warwick, Pawtucket, Cranston and I-95/I-195
providers.notes: Official RIDOT lists camera names and public streams; independent direct URL, terms, coordinates and freshness must be validated before ingestion.

providers.coverage: Wilmington, Newark DE, Dover and DE interstates
providers.media: Public camera map, direct source requires verification
providers.notes: DelDOT FirstMap traffic device camera metadata layer 26 provides names, road/intersection, equipment status and geometry. Projection is EPSG:26957; request outSR=4326. No live-media URLs are published in this layer. This is on a firstmaptest host: confirm production authority before operational use.

providers.agency: New England 511 / state DOT partner map
providers.coverage: Maine, New Hampshire and Vermont; Portland, Bangor, Manchester, Concord, Burlington
providers.notes: Official New England 511 serves ME/NH/VT public camera and RWIS locations. Public viewing is confirmed, but an unrestricted, documented developer media API and its redistribution rights were not verified. Do not scrape browser internals.

region_priority: Northeast first: individual cameras must have provider-issued coordinates and health before automatic selection
media_policy: No operator camera is auto-fetched merely because public metadata lists an image or HLS URL. Require provider reuse authorization, real camera coordinates, and a current direct-media probe.
